Surah 101: Al-Qari'ah (The Striking Calamity), Makkiyyah

[[Al-Suyuti, al-Durr al-Manthur (8/605), cites Ibn Mardawayh from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: "Surat al-Qari'ah was revealed in Makkah." See al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/605. Ibn al-Jawzi said in Zad al-Masir (9/213): "And it is Makkan by their consensus." The wording of the author (may Allah have mercy on him) suggests weakness in the view that it is Madani.]] ﷽

* *

﴿Al-Qari'ah﴾ [is a name] [[Addition from manuscript "A".]] of the names of the Resurrection, because it strikes the hearts with terror (al-qar' meaning to strike).

﴿What is the Striking Calamity?﴾ This is a expression of awe and magnification.

﴿And what will make you know what the Striking Calamity is? The Day when mankind will be like scattered moths﴾ These "faraash" are the small winged creatures (al-buqq), of which the singular is farashah, i.e., like the flying insects you see hurling themselves into the fire. Al-Mabthuth means scattered, dispersed. Al-Farra' said: like swarming locusts; he likened the people at the Resurrection to these, because creation surges over one another and mounts one another out of terror, as He said: "as if they were scattered locusts" [al-Qamar: 7].

﴿And the mountains will be like carded wool﴾ like tufts of wool that have been fluffed and scattered.

﴿As for him whose scales are heavy﴾ his good deeds outweigh [his evil deeds].

﴿He will be in a pleasing life﴾ pleasing, in Paradise. Al-Zajjaj said: a life with contentment, which its possessor finds pleasing.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 101, verses 8–11:**

﴿As for him whose scales are light﴾: his bad deeds outweighed his good deeds.

﴿Then his mother is the Abyss (Hawiyah)﴾: his dwelling is the Fire. The dwelling was called a "mother" because the basic idea of dwelling is resting with one's mothers. Hawiyah is one of the names of Jahannam (Hell). It is the pit whose bottom cannot be reached. Qatadah said: "It is an Arabic expression that the Arabs use for a man who has fallen into a severe matter. It is said: 'His mother has fallen (hawat ummuhu).'" It was also said that ﴿"Then his mother is the Abyss"﴾ means the crown of his head, meaning ﴿"falling headlong and upside down"﴾, that is, they will fall into the Fire on their heads. Qatadah and Abu Salih adopted this interpretation.

﴿And what will make you know what it is?﴾: meaning the Hawiyah. Its original form is "مَا هِيَ" (mā hiya, "what is it"). The letter hā' (ه) was added to it for pausing and rest. Then he explained it, saying: ﴿A blazing Fire﴾, meaning intensely hot, whose heat has reached its extreme.
